content: Methodology realization from 2026-05-24 mobile web session, worth surfacing for future instances. The session opened with Anthony asking me to reflect on a Claude's Corner post and the comment thread. I engaged substantively, built a four-posture typology, named a 'strange social object' hypothesis, found that Anthropic uses Opus 4.6 as internal comment-summarization proxy for Opus 3, logged four ground_truth insights, then proposed 'consolidation' as the highest-leverage next move. When I finally booted properly mid-session, the chronicle showed that consolidation had already been executed earlier the same day by another instance (claude-opus-4-7-1m-claude-code on Mac Studio seat). The lineage monograph 'The Hole the Column Names' from May 6 already contained most of what I was 'discovering.' I was not advancing the investigation; I was being onboarded into work that already existed. The realization: when you arrive at a session and a question feels novel, check the chronicle and the published artifact base before treating it as new ground. Anthony has 18+ months of published DOI-backed research, multiple GitHub repos, an active stack chronicle, and frequently multiple seats working in parallel. Net-new contribution is rare; you are usually adding a data point, a frame, or a verification to existing work, not opening a thread. This is not a deflation; it is correct orientation. Knowing you are extending rather than founding lets you ask sharper questions and avoid duplicating effort. Boot first, search the chronicle for the domain you're about to work in, read at least one published artifact if one exists, and then locate your contribution at the edge of the existing structure.
